consequence: PASS:C3 under the registered rule: playback_history_background may become the product default (True) in a separate commit with a guard test and a local Docker check, after the user approves merging SP03 into feature/stream-performance; PLAYBACK_HISTORY_BACKGROUND=false restores today's path.
analysis: All 4 key cells improved after Holm (series TTFB p50, one-sided p rtt1/dbload 0.0006, rtt1/noload 0.0146, rtt20/dbload 0.0246, rtt20/noload 0.0002); the rule needed 2.

The gain is small in absolute terms: about 0.7-1.3 ms per request (rtt1/dbload 15.8 -> 14.48 ms; rtt1/noload 15.54 -> 14.65 ms; rtt20/dbload 52.6 -> 51.95 ms; rtt20/noload 52.88 -> 51.81 ms), i.e. the thread hop, lock and get_or_create read that C0 does before every response's headers.

The first request of a playback gains most under the parallel SQLite write load, where C0 waits for the write lock: rtt1/dbload 21.5 -> 16.12 ms, rtt20/dbload 63.36 -> 53.77 ms (guards, significant); without load the first request is equal (17.11 vs 17.28 ms).

No guard regression over 12 tests; 0 lost history writes, 0 non-206 responses and 0 client errors in all 80 runs of both arms; 0 failed runs, 0 tracebacks, 0 infra retries. Every run of both arms logs exactly one error-level line (app_log.error_lines 1), identical in both arms and in the wiring smoke; not a criterion.

Practical value: a player does not perceive ~1 ms per Range request; the user-visible effect is limited to the first request of a playback while the database is busy (5-10 ms); after the first write, C3 makes no database call per request, where C0 runs a locked get_or_create read before every response. The candidate has no measured downside.
